protocol.purpose: test nonlinear coefficient heads and shared wider projectors at equal parameter budget, with a fixed-width tying control
protocol.calibration_metric: mean highest-FP32 fixed-input adapter-delta single-step update RMS across six blocks, steps 50/100/250/500 and seeds 65/66
protocol.selection: closest absolute log(mean update / target); excludes loss, validation, FID and class agreement
protocol.correction: clip(previous multiplier * target / previous update metric, 1/16, 16)
protocol.gain_design: fixed 1/sqrt(8) throughout; independent affine r8/s16 is the update anchor

auxiliary_classifier.purpose: fixed auxiliary evaluator of generated requested-class agreement
auxiliary_classifier.retention: one frozen evaluator and its compact training records until explicitly removed

protocol.estimated_new_gpu_hours: 1.5–3 aggregate including bounded calibration, validation, diagnostics and final evaluations; startup additional
protocol.retention: compact source/configs/seeds/splits/metrics/logs/audits/plots until explicitly removed; no grids, model/evaluator weights or generated datasets
limits: Two-seed 5k quality screen, not longer confirmation or statistical significance.
Independent affine/silu s16, two-group affine/silu s48, and all-shared affine s96 have equal adapter and total parameter counts.
Two-group affine s16 is a fixed-width tying control; the full sharing/width/nonlinearity factorial is not tested.
One shared module per group; unique parameters and per-layer diagnostics are separately audited.
The same broadcast condition ties the conditional transform within each group, while base blocks and AdaLN/gates remain independent.
At equal affine budget G*s is fixed; lower group count does not establish lower total generation FLOPs or speed.
Rates are selected only on aggregate early function updates, not loss or generated quality; matching may drift across seeds/layers/time.
Calibration seeds 65/66 and screen seeds 67/68 are fresh relative to previous quality studies.
FID uses 5k images and a fixed sampling seed; classifier agreement is a frozen proxy.
Raw-model diagnostics and EMA quality concern different states; fixed-probe operator Frobenius norms do not establish variance preservation.
No output normalization, larger MLP/trunk, layer embeddings, partial decoder sharing, new ViT/LM/retrieval or structured operators are tested.
Concurrent eager training is not isolated timing or an equal-time comparison; dedicated speed work stays deferred.
No automatic longer confirmation is launched by this screen.

limitations: One fixed validation split; seed spread is not a confidence interval or test-set estimate.
FID uses held-out train images and finite sample counts; not published 50k-image FID.
Wrong-class loss measures sensitivity/use, not generated class accuracy.
External condition is a single class/time vector; sequence-conditioned cross-attention is not evaluated.
Concurrent throughput shares CPU/storage; matrix FLOPs omit non-matmul work and backward.
Generative evaluation time includes sampling and FID feature/statistic computation; isolated inference throughput is not measured.
Each screen has its own declared LR/initialization recipe; optimal rates are not established without bracketing.

limits: Two-seed 5k quality screen, not longer confirmation or statistical significance.
Independent affine/silu s16, two-group affine/silu s48, and all-shared affine s96 have equal adapter and total parameter counts.
Two-group affine s16 is a fixed-width tying control; the full sharing/width/nonlinearity factorial is not tested.
One shared module per group; unique parameters and per-layer diagnostics are separately audited.
The same broadcast condition ties the conditional transform within each group, while base blocks and AdaLN/gates remain independent.
At equal affine budget G*s is fixed; lower group count does not establish lower total generation FLOPs or speed.
Rates are selected only on aggregate early function updates, not loss or generated quality; matching may drift across seeds/layers/time.
Calibration seeds 65/66 and screen seeds 67/68 are fresh relative to previous quality studies.
FID uses 5k images and a fixed sampling seed; classifier agreement is a frozen proxy.
Raw-model diagnostics and EMA quality concern different states; fixed-probe operator Frobenius norms do not establish variance preservation.
No output normalization, larger MLP/trunk, layer embeddings, partial decoder sharing, new ViT/LM/retrieval or structured operators are tested.
Concurrent eager training is not isolated timing or an equal-time comparison; dedicated speed work stays deferred.
No automatic longer confirmation is launched by this screen.
